title: Tissue Analysis Using QCL-based Infrared Laser Imaging
content: Infrared spectroscopy has been widely used to study biological systems for decades, allowing researchers to analyze the chemical composition and structure of biomolecules including lipids, proteins, nucleic acids and carbohydrates within the sample [1]. IR imaging can be used for biomedical applications such as tissue characterization to understand basic functions of organisms as well as to detect abnormalities [2, 3]. Acquiring comprehensive information on heterogeneous and complex biological systems with unique chemical specificity and spatial resolution provides a powerful tool for early-stage disease detection and monitoring. In the past, imaging whole tissue sections at high spatial resolution (≤10 μm pixel size) has required extensive acquisition times. New emerging QCL-based infrared laser microscopy has revolutionized the application of IR Spectroscopy in biomedical field by increasing the imaging speed by orders of magnitude when compared to conventional FT-IR imaging [4].
